env.name: AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH
env.note: In the template's docker options, so the server never starts without a token. A pod the studio creates gets its own token, which wins over this one.

env.name: AITK_CORS_ORIGINS
env.note: Lets your studio call the server from the browser.

quickpod.docker_options: -p 8675:8675 -e AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH=<a long random token> -e AITK_CORS_ORIGINS=<your studio origin>

fields.label: Docker Image Path
fields.note: The tag goes in the path: there is no separate tag field.

fields.label: Disk Space
fields.note: GB. Only the default: you pick the size again at launch.

fields.label: Launch Mode
fields.note: Uses the image's entrypoint, which starts the server.

steps: Sign in at console.quickpod.io and add credit under Settings. For the studio to create pods for you later, a key under Settings → Secure API keys needs Pods read, Pods write, Templates read and Profile read.
Open Templates and click Create New Template.
Fill in the fields above. Leave Private Docker Repository unticked, and leave Docker Entrypoint Run Options and On Start Script empty.

Paste the docker options into Docker Options. Keep both parts: -p 8675:8675 publishes the port, and AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH keeps the server from starting without a token. If you change the token, use only letters, digits, - and _: QuickPod silently drops other characters from docker options.

Click Create Template. On GPU Search, pick an offer with a max CUDA of 13.0 or newer on an RTX 30-series, A100 or newer GPU: the image needs a driver for CUDA 13.0 or newer (580+). On an older host the image fails, and the rental still bills. Choose aitk headless under My Templates and click Create.
On Pods, wait for running and click Connect. Under Exposed Ports, the 8675 row has an HTTPS link (https://<pod id>-8675.proxy.quickpod.io/) and an HTTP link (http://<ip>:<port>).
When it shows running, copy its URL and add it on the Servers page with the same token.

env.name: AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH
env.note: The server asks for it on every request. A RunPod secret works too: {{ RUNPOD_SECRET_aitk_token }}.

env.name: AITK_CORS_ORIGINS
env.note: Lets your studio call the server from the browser.

env.name: HF_TOKEN
env.note: Optional, for gated base models: save your Hugging Face token as the RunPod secret hf_token first.

runpod.env_block:
AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH=<a long random token>
AITK_CORS_ORIGINS=<your studio origin>

fields.label: Container Image
fields.note: A public image, so Container Registry Credentials stay empty.

fields.label: Container Disk
fields.note: GB for models, datasets and checkpoints. It is wiped when the pod stops, so keep results on a remote and terminate the pod when you are done.

steps: Sign in at console.runpod.io, open Templates and click New Template.
Set Template Type to Pod and Compute type to NVIDIA GPU, then fill in the fields above. Leave Container Start Command empty: the image starts the server itself.
Under Environment Variables, add the variables above.
For gated base models, also add HF_TOKEN = {{ RUNPOD_SECRET_hf_token }} after saving your Hugging Face token as the secret hf_token under Settings → Secrets.
Click Save Template.

Open Pods, click Deploy, set the CUDA version filter to 13.0 or newer and pick an RTX 30-series, A100 or newer GPU: the image needs a driver for CUDA 13.0 or newer (580+). On an older host the image fails, and the rental still bills. Click Change Template, choose aitk headless and click Deploy On-Demand.
When the pod shows running, open Connect → HTTP Service: the 8675 row links to https://<pod id>-8675.proxy.runpod.net.
When it shows running, copy its URL and add it on the Servers page with the same token.

env.name: AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH
env.note: Under Account → Environment Variables, so it stays out of the template. Or, with Template Visibility Private, as -e AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH=<a long random token> in Docker Options. An account-wide value also reaches the servers the studio creates for you.

env.name: OPEN_BUTTON_PORT
env.note: Points the instance's Open button at the server.

env.name: AITK_CORS_ORIGINS

env.name: HF_TOKEN
env.note: Optional, for gated base models. Also under Account → Environment Variables.

fields.label: Image Path:Tag
fields.note: The full registry path. Another tag works too.

fields.label: Select Launch Mode
fields.note: Runs the image as built, which starts the server.

fields.label: Extra Filters
fields.note: Only hosts that can give port 8675 a public port, with a driver for CUDA 13.0 or newer (580+) and an RTX 30-series, A100 or newer GPU.

fields.label: Disk Space
fields.note: GB, fixed for the life of the instance.

steps: Open Account → Environment Variables (cloud.vast.ai/account/) and add AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH = <a long random token>. Vast puts it into every instance, so it stays out of the template. Or, with Template Visibility Private, add -e AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH=<a long random token> to Docker Options instead. An account-wide AI_TOOLKIT_AUTH also reaches the servers the studio creates for you, which get their own token, so use the template if you also create servers from the studio. Add HF_TOKEN under Account → Environment Variables for gated base models.
Open Templates (cloud.vast.ai/templates/), click + New and stay on the Config tab.
Fill in the fields above and paste the docker options into Docker Options.

Click Create & Use, pick an offer and click RENT. The Extra Filters above keep the offers to hosts with a driver for CUDA 13.0 or newer (580+) and an RTX 30-series, A100 or newer GPU. On an older host the image fails, and the rental still bills.

When the instance shows running, open IP Port Info: the line ending in -> 8675/tcp gives the URL http://<ip>:<port>. It is plain http only, so the token crosses the internet unencrypted, and a studio served over https cannot call it directly: use the studio the server serves at /studio/.
When it shows running, copy its URL and add it on the Servers page with the same token.
